name: _sparse_sum
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim: `aten::_sparse_sum.dim(Tensor self, int[1] dim) -> Tensor`. This representative overload is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full overload, keyword-argument, return, error, mutation and aliasing contract, and its coverage must never be narrowed to this one signature. All registered ATen schemas of aten::_sparse_sum, listed verbatim: `aten::_sparse_sum.dim(Tensor self, int[1] dim) -> Tensor`; `aten::_sparse_sum.dim_out(Tensor self, int[1] dim, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!)`; `aten::_sparse_sum(Tensor self) -> Tensor`; `aten::_sparse_sum.dtype(Tensor self, *, ScalarType dtype) -> Tensor`; `aten::_sparse_sum.dim_dtype(Tensor self, int[1] dim, *, ScalarType dtype) -> Tensor`. Semantics derived from the tests: _sparse_sum reduces the stored values of a sparse COO tensor, coalescing duplicate coordinates internally; the default form (no dim) fully reduces to a dense 0-dim result, while reducing a subset of dims keeps a sparse COO result; an empty dim list leaves the operand shape unchanged and a 0-dim operand accepts only the empty dim list; dim entries may be negative within the operand rank; integer stored dtypes promote to int64 on full reduction; the dtype overload takes a keyword-only ScalarType target and its result is compared against the native reference; the .dim_dtype overload combines a dim subset with a cast target, casting the stored values before reducing, and works for fp8 operands; the keyword-only .dim_out form writes into and returns the caller-provided buffer (aliased and mutated). Out-of-range or duplicate dims, a dim on a 0-dim operand, and dense input are rejected by pytest; on NVIDIA CUDA pytest also rejects fp8 stored values for the coalescing default form, while the source records the same missing fp8 kernel for the .dim and .dtype forms although no pytest case exercises them with fp8.
